# Finding Complete Fulfillment in God

### A Discourse by Sri Daya Mata

*Beloved President and Sanghamata of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India*

---

### The Eternal Thirst of the Soul

In this sacred discourse, Sri Daya Mata, one of the foremost disciples of Paramahansa Yogananda, speaks directly to the universal longing of every human heart. Each soul is searching for complete, unalloyed, and everlasting happiness. We seek it in human relationships, in professional success, in material acquisitions, and in the fleeting pleasures of this world. Yet, as Daya Mataji tenderly reminds us, these external objects are only pale reflections of the true Source of all joy.

Our hearts remain restless and unfulfilled until they rest in God. It is only in the silent, blissful communion with the Divine Mother that the soul find its true home, its ultimate security, and its eternal satisfaction.

> "The world promises much but gives very little in return. It is only when you find God that you will experience a love that never fades, a peace that cannot be shaken, and a joy that is forever new."

### The Delusion of Worldly Pleasures

We are taught from childhood to look outside of ourselves for happiness. We believe that if we can only find the perfect companion, the ideal career, or sufficient material wealth, we will finally be at peace. But the law of this dualistic universe is one of constant change and impermanence. Everything that has a beginning must also have an end. When we place our ultimate hope for fulfillment in that which is transient, we inevitably pave the way for disappointment, grief, and spiritual exhaustion.

Paramahansa Yogananda often warned his disciples not to become entangled in the web of *maya* (cosmic delusion). Sri Daya Mata reiterates this timeless wisdom, emphasizing that we must look beyond the shifting shadows of creation to find the unchanging Creator. It is not that we must renounce our duties or abandon our loved ones; rather, we must perform our actions with our minds anchored in the Divine, realizing that He is the doer, the giver, and the ultimate recipient of all our love.

### Cultivating the Intimacy of Silent Prayer

To find complete fulfillment in God, we must cultivate an intimate, personal relationship with Him. He is not a distant, judgmental deity sitting upon a cloud; He is closer than our very breath, nearer than our hands and feet. He is the loving Father, the compassionate Divine Mother, the dearest Friend, and the beloved Guide.

Sri Daya Mata encourages us to talk to God in the language of our own hearts. We do not need elaborate, formal prayers. What He desires most is our sincere, childlike devotion. When we pray, we should speak to Him as we would to our closest companion, sharing our joys, our struggles, our fears, and our deepest aspirations.

> "Do not seek Him only with your intellect. Seek Him with your love. Cry for Him in the silence of the night, and say to Him: 'My Lord, I want nothing but Thee. Reveal Thyself unto me.' If you call to Him with that deep, earnest yearning of your soul, He cannot remain hidden from you."

### The Power of Meditation and Kriya Yoga

While devotional prayer prepares the ground, it is through the scientific practice of meditation, particularly Kriya Yoga, that we actually enter the temple of His presence. Sri Daya Mata emphasizes the importance of daily, systematic meditation as taught by our Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda. 

By quieting the restless activity of the mind and senses, we draw our energy inward, tapping into the fountain of peace that flows eternally within the spiritual center of the brain. In that deep silence, the ego-self dissolves, and we realize our oneness with the Infinite. The soul then experiences *Satchidananda*—Ever-existing, Ever-conscious, Ever-new Joy. Once you have tasted that divine nectar, the fleeting pleasures of this world lose their power to charm or delude you.

### Active Will and Divine Surrender

To attain this state of complete fulfillment, we must employ our active, dynamic will. Sri Daya Mata explains that spiritual progress is not for the passive or the lukewarm. We must make a conscious, daily effort to seek God, even when the mind is restless or the world clamors for our attention.

At the same time, this active effort must be balanced with absolute surrender to His will. True surrender is not a sign of weakness; it is the highest form of spiritual courage. It is the conscious alignment of our individual will with the cosmic, omnipotent Will of God. When we surrender our lives completely into His hands, we are freed from all anxiety and fear, knowing that He is guiding every step of our journey back to His heart.

### Practical Guidelines for Daily Spiritual Living

To integrate these teachings into our daily lives, Sri Daya Mata suggests several practical habits:

* **Begin and End the Day with God:** Dedicate the first moments of the morning and the last moments before sleep to quiet meditation and prayer. Establish a sacred connection with Him before engaging with the world.
* **Practice the Presence of God:** Throughout the day, keep a silent current of devotion running in the background of your mind. Mentally repeat His name, or whisper, "I love Thee, Lord; guide me, protect me, guide my thoughts and actions."
* **Perform Unselfish Service:** Serve others with the understanding that you are serving the Divine spark within them. This purifies the heart and expands our capacity to love.
* **Meditation over Speculation:** Dedicate more time to the actual practice of meditation rather than reading about spiritual truths. Intellectual knowledge alone cannot satisfy the soul; only direct experience can.
* **Cultivate Even-Mindedness:** Welcome both joys and trials with an equal mind, viewing every circumstance as a gift from the Divine Mother designed to help your soul grow.

### A Prayer for Divine Union

Let us close this reading by taking a deep, quiet breath, drawing our attention inward to the Christ center between the eyebrows, and offering this prayer with all the love of our hearts:

*O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Friend, beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda!*  
*Thou art my ultimate refuge, my only goal, and my eternal home. Teach me to seek Thee first above all things. Cleanse my heart of all material desires, that I may be a fit temple for Thy presence. Fill my soul with Thy love, Thy joy, and Thy unshakeable peace. Guide my steps, lead me from darkness to light, from delusion to Truth, and from the illusion of separation into perfect, eternal union with Thee.*  

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
rawText: In this sacred discourse, Sri Daya Mata, the beloved disciple of Paramahansa Yogananda, guides us on how to find complete fulfillment in God. She explains that the human soul is in a state of constant restlessness because it tries to find permanent joy in impermanent, worldly things. Whether in human relationships, wealth, or professional success, these external experiences can never fully satisfy the deepest yearning of the heart, which is designed for God alone. Sri Daya Mata encourages us to establish a deeply personal, intimate, and devotional relationship with the Divine Mother and Heavenly Father. Through sincere, childlike prayer, the active use of our dynamic will, and the daily, scientific practice of Kriya Yoga meditation, we can quiet our minds and experience the direct presence of God. By practicing His presence throughout the day and surrendering our lives to His cosmic will, we transition from restless delusion to a state of ever-new, eternal joy. This pathway of love, meditation, and unselfish service is the only way to attain complete fulfillment and ultimate peace.
